plan: In a sealed-bid, second-price auction with independent private values, bidding one’s true value is a dominant strategy that maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. My value is 3, which is low on the 0–49 scale. Overbidding risks winning at a price above my value if rivals bid just below; underbidding risks losing when I would have positive surplus. With no informative history and only one round, there is no beneficial learning or collusion. I will bid exactly my value, to the nearest $0.1 increment.

Second-price sealed-bid with independent private values. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid truthfully: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Shading below 24 risks losing when winning would yield positive surplus; bidding above 24 risks paying more than value if outbid only slightly. No prior rounds to learn from and values are redrawn, so no history-based adjustment. With 3 bidders, truthful bidding remains optimal. I will bid exactly my value, 24.0, which ensures winning whenever the second-highest value is below 24 and paying that second-highest bid.

Bidding above 11 risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds your value, yielding negative profit; bidding below 11 risks losing when you would have profited (second-highest < 11). There’s no exploitable history in round 1 of 1, and values are independently redrawn each round. Therefore, bid exactly your value. ]
